Toolbar.start.note: Label of the toolbar's start button (left, after the machine's name) while the machine is off, not started or suspended.

Toolbar.start.title.message: Start the machine, or resume it if it's suspended.
Toolbar.start.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Start button (the machine is off, not started or suspended).

Toolbar.retry.note: Label of the toolbar's start button after the machine failed to start.

Toolbar.retry.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Retry button (after the machine failed to start).

Toolbar.restart.note: Label of the toolbar's start button while the machine runs (or is starting): it resets it.

Toolbar.restart.title.message: Forcibly power off the machine and start it again.
Toolbar.restart.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Restart button: a reset without the guest's shutdown.

Toolbar.view.screen.note: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the toolbar's view button that shows the machine's screen alone.

Toolbar.view.terminal.note: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the toolbar's view button that shows the machine's serial terminal alone.

Toolbar.view.both.note: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the toolbar's view button that shows the screen and the serial terminal side by side.

Toolbar.name.note: The product's name, at the toolbar's left end (the page's heading).

Toolbar.machines.title.message: Show the machines stored in this browser, with their settings, disks, overlays, and snapshots.
Toolbar.machines.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Machines button, which opens the Machines page.

Toolbar.machines.note: Label of the toolbar's first button: it opens the Machines page (the machines kept in this browser).

Toolbar.powerOff.note: Screen-reader name of the toolbar's Power off button (a stop icon), shown while the machine runs.

Toolbar.powerOff.title.message: Forcibly power off the machine, like pulling the plug. Shut the guest down first for a clean stop.
Toolbar.powerOff.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Power off button (a stop icon).

Toolbar.suspend.note: Screen-reader name of the toolbar's Suspend button (zzz icon), shown for a machine whose disk keeps its changes in this browser.

Toolbar.suspend.title.message: Stop the machine and keep its memory in this browser. The next start resumes it where it left off.
Toolbar.suspend.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Suspend button (zzz icon).

Toolbar.snapshot.title.message: Take a snapshot of the running machine and keep it in this browser. The machine pauses for a moment, then runs on.
Toolbar.snapshot.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Snapshot button for a machine kept in this browser.

Toolbar.snapshot.title.file.message: Take a snapshot of the running machine and save it to a file. The machine pauses for a moment, then runs on.
Toolbar.snapshot.title.file.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Snapshot button for a machine that isn't kept in this browser (the snapshot is saved as a file).

Toolbar.snapshot.note: Label of the toolbar's Snapshot button: it takes a snapshot of the running machine.

Toolbar.load.title.message: Load a snapshot, returning the machine to the state it was in when the snapshot was taken.
Toolbar.load.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Load snapshot menu button (history icon, after Snapshot).

Toolbar.load.latest.note: Heading over the list of the machine's latest snapshots in the toolbar's Load snapshot menu.

Toolbar.load.orphaned.title.message: This snapshot was taken when the machine had other settings or disks. It can't be restored onto the machine as it is now.
Toolbar.load.orphaned.title.note: Tooltip of a snapshot shown disabled in the toolbar's Load snapshot menu: the machine's settings or disks changed since it was taken.

Toolbar.load.restore.title.note: Tooltip of a snapshot in the toolbar's Load snapshot menu; a click restores it. {{name}} is the snapshot's name.

Toolbar.load.none.message: No snapshots yet. Snapshot takes one.
Toolbar.load.none.note: Line in the toolbar's Load snapshot menu when the machine has no snapshot kept; Snapshot is the toolbar's button that takes one.

Toolbar.load.all.note: Item of the toolbar's Load snapshot menu: opens the machine's Snapshots tab on the Machines page.

Toolbar.load.file.note: Item of the toolbar's Load snapshot menu: picks a snapshot file to restore.

Toolbar.views.note: Screen-reader name of the toolbar's group of view buttons (screen, serial terminal, both).

Toolbar.screen.title.message: Set the size of the machine's screen.
Toolbar.screen.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Screen menu button (machines with a virtio-gpu).

Toolbar.screen.size.note: Label of the screen size dropdown in the toolbar's Screen menu (Fit the window, or a fixed size).

Toolbar.screen.fit.note: Choice in the toolbar's Screen menu's Size dropdown: the screen follows the page's size.

Toolbar.screen.hidpi.title.message: Draw the guest in device pixels instead of CSS pixels. The picture is sharper on a HiDPI screen, and text is smaller unless the guest's desktop scales it; the screen's EDID gives the desktop the screen's physical size to scale by.
Toolbar.screen.hidpi.title.note: Tooltip of the HiDPI checkbox in the toolbar's Screen menu.

Toolbar.screen.hidpi.note: Checkbox in the toolbar's Screen menu: the screen in device pixels.

Toolbar.screen.hint.message: A text console (fbcon) keeps the size it started with. A new size takes effect at the next boot, and the console is centred until then. A desktop takes the size when it starts; whether it follows a later change depends on its compositor (sway doesn't).
Toolbar.screen.hint.note: Fine print at the foot of the toolbar's Screen menu: when a new size takes effect.

Toolbar.keys.title.message: Send key combinations that the browser keeps for itself to the guest.
Toolbar.keys.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Keys menu button (keyboard icon): it sends key combinations the browser would take.

Toolbar.keys.ctrlAltDel.note: Item of the toolbar's Keys menu: sends Ctrl+Alt+Delete to the machine. The keys' names as the keyboard labels them.

Toolbar.keys.ctrlAlt.note: Heading in the toolbar's Keys menu over the row of F1–F12 buttons, each sending Ctrl+Alt and that key.

Toolbar.keys.fkey.title.note: Tooltip and screen-reader name of a function key button in the toolbar's Keys menu. {{n}} is the function key's number (1 to 12).

Toolbar.keys.fkey.note: A function key button in the toolbar's Keys menu, under the Ctrl+Alt+ heading. {{n}} is the function key's number (1 to 12).

Toolbar.mouse.title.locked.message: Mouse lock is on, and the machine has the mouse. Press Esc to release it.
Toolbar.mouse.title.locked.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Mouse lock menu button while the screen holds the mouse.

Toolbar.mouse.title.on.message: Mouse lock is on. Click the screen to give the machine the mouse.
Toolbar.mouse.title.on.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Mouse lock menu button while the lock is on but the screen doesn't hold the mouse.

Toolbar.mouse.title.message: Mouse lock. Turn it on to give the machine the mouse, every button included, when you click the screen.
Toolbar.mouse.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Mouse lock menu button while the lock is off.

Toolbar.mouse.lock.title.message: When you click the screen, the machine gets the mouse. Every button reaches it, the back and forward ones included, and the browser hides its pointer. Press Esc to release the mouse.
Toolbar.mouse.lock.title.note: Tooltip of the Lock the mouse on a click checkbox in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu.

Toolbar.mouse.lock.message: Lock the mouse on a click
Toolbar.mouse.lock.note: Checkbox in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu: turns the mouse lock on.

Toolbar.mouse.pointer.title.message: The pointer moves as it does unlocked, at your computer's speed, and stays within the screen.
Toolbar.mouse.pointer.title.note: Tooltip of the Pointer choice in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu.

Toolbar.mouse.pointer.message: Pointer: the same speed as unlocked
Toolbar.mouse.pointer.note: Radio choice in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu: how the locked mouse moves the machine's pointer (the default).

Toolbar.mouse.raw.title.message: Send the mouse's own motion to the machine's relative mouse, unbounded by the screen, for games that turn with the mouse. The guest's mouse settings set its speed.
Toolbar.mouse.raw.title.note: Tooltip of the Raw choice in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu, when the machine has a relative mouse.

Toolbar.mouse.raw.title.noMouse.message: This machine has no relative mouse, so the lock moves the pointer. Turn on Mouse in the machine's settings to use Raw.
Toolbar.mouse.raw.title.noMouse.note: Tooltip of the Raw choice in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu, disabled because the machine has no relative mouse (the Mouse setting on the Machines page).

Toolbar.mouse.raw.note: Radio choice in the toolbar's Mouse lock menu: the mouse's own motion to the machine's relative mouse.

Toolbar.mouse.hint.message: Press Esc to release the mouse. In Raw, the guest's own mouse settings set the speed.
Toolbar.mouse.hint.note: Fine print at the foot of the toolbar's Mouse lock menu, for a machine with a relative mouse.

Toolbar.mouse.hint.noMouse.message: Press Esc to release the mouse. In Raw, the guest's own mouse settings set the speed. Raw needs Mouse turned on in the machine's settings.
Toolbar.mouse.hint.noMouse.note: Fine print at the foot of the toolbar's Mouse lock menu, for a machine without a relative mouse (the Mouse setting on the Machines page).

Toolbar.fullscreen.note: Screen-reader name of the toolbar's Full screen button.

Toolbar.fullscreen.title.message: Show the machine full screen. Browser shortcuts such as Ctrl+W and Ctrl+T, and Esc, go to the machine; hold Esc to leave.
Toolbar.fullscreen.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Full screen button.

Toolbar.size.title.message: Set the machine's vCPUs, RAM, and graphics. A change takes effect when the machine restarts.
Toolbar.size.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's Machine menu button (CPU icon), shown for a machine that isn't kept in this browser.

Toolbar.size.cpus.note: Label of the vCPU count dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu.

Toolbar.size.cpu_one.note: A choice of the Processors dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu: {{count}} is the number of virtual CPUs.

Toolbar.size.cpu_other.note: A choice of the Processors dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu: {{count}} is the number of virtual CPUs.

Toolbar.size.ram.note: Label of the RAM size dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu (its choices are sizes in MiB or GiB).

Toolbar.size.gpu.title.message: 3D gives the guest OpenGL ES through this browser's WebGL2 (virgl). 2D is a plain framebuffer.
Toolbar.size.gpu.title.note: Tooltip of the Graphics dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu.

Toolbar.size.gpu.note: Label of the graphics dropdown (3D or 2D) in the toolbar's Machine menu.

Toolbar.size.gpu.3d.note: Choice of the Graphics dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu: 3D through virgl on the browser's WebGL2.

Toolbar.size.gpu.2d.note: Choice of the Graphics dropdown in the toolbar's Machine menu: a plain framebuffer.

Toolbar.size.apply.note: Button in the toolbar's Machine menu: restarts the machine with the size chosen.

Toolbar.size.hint.message: This size is kept in this browser. A suspended machine resumes with the size it had; Boot instead starts it from its disk with this one.
Toolbar.size.hint.note: Fine print at the foot of the toolbar's Machine menu.

main.gpuLock.noWebgl2.message: This browser has no WebGL2, so only 2D is available.
main.gpuLock.noWebgl2.note: Tooltip of the Machine menu's Graphics choice (the toolbar), turned off because the browser has no WebGL2.

main.gpuLock.address.note: Tooltip of the Machine menu's Graphics choice (the toolbar), turned off because the page's address sets it; {{gpu}} is the address's value.
